source_title: KDIGO 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in Chronic Kidney Disease (Recommendation 4.1.1, Figure 27); GLUCOPHAGE/GLUCOPHAGE XR (metformin) US prescribing information; JANUVIA (sitagliptin) US prescribing information
source_org_or_authors: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Diabetes Work Group; Bristol-Myers Squibb (Glucophage label, FDA NDA 020357/021202); Merck Sharp & Dohme (Januvia label)
source_year: 2022 (KDIGO); Glucophage label rev. April 2017; Januvia label effective 2024-11-14
source_identifier: doi:10.1016/j.kint.2022.06.008 (PMID 36272764; Kidney Int 2022;102(5S):S1-S127; PDF https://kdigo.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/KDIGO-2022-Clinical-Practice-Guideline-for-Diabetes-Management-in-CKD.pdf); https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/020357s037s039,021202s021s023lbl.pdf (Reference ID 4079189); DailyMed setid f85a48d0-0407-4c50-b0fa-7673a160bf01 (Januvia)
supporting_text: KDIGO Recommendation 4.1.1: "We recommend treating patients with T2D, CKD, and an eGFR ≥30 ml/min per 1.73 m2 with metformin (1B)." KDIGO Figure 27: "eGFR < 30 Stop metformin; do not initiate metformin". Glucophage label: "GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR is contraindicated in patients with an eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 ... Initiation of GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR is not recommended in patients with eGFR between 30-45 mL/min/1.73 m2." Januvia label: "For patients with severe renal impairment (eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) or with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis, the dose of JANUVIA is 25 mg once daily."
simplifications: Default 'start metformin' applied to every patient with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and eGFR ≥30. KDIGO Recommendation 4.1.1 concerns T2D with CKD, and KDIGO Figure 27 starts at half the dose at eGFR 30-44 (doses omitted).

Metformin alone as the default. For T2D with CKD, KDIGO's first-line therapy is metformin plus an SGLT2 inhibitor (Rec 1.3.1, eGFR ≥20, 1A; Figure 23). ADA Standards of Care 2026 Rec 9.6 says to consider combination therapy for initial treatment.

Alternative fixed to sitagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor; its label gives 25 mg once daily at eGFR <30). Neither the guideline nor the metformin label names it as the replacement, and it is not the preferred agent. KDIGO recommends an SGLT2 inhibitor down to eGFR 20 regardless of metformin (Rec 1.3.1, 1A). It recommends a long-acting GLP-1 RA for patients not at target on, or unable to use, metformin and an SGLT2i (Rec 4.2.1, 1B). KDIGO Figure 23 marks GLP-1 RA as preferred and lists DPP-4 inhibitors among the other additional drugs. ADA 2026 Rec 9.11 says that at eGFR <30 'a GLP-1 RA is preferred for glycemic management'.
Only the eGFR criterion kept; other metformin contraindications and precautions (metabolic acidosis, hypersensitivity, iodinated contrast, hepatic impairment) omitted.
Applicability: current eGFR only (counts_past=false).
contradictions: eGFR 30-45 band: US metformin labels state 'Initiation of GLUCOPHAGE or GLUCOPHAGE XR is not recommended in patients with eGFR between 30-45 mL/min/1.73 m2' (the same wording is in current generic labeling, e.g. DailyMed setid c3dfa8a1-d10a-4a1a-8eba-5f4e2a5a2949, effective 2026-09-25). The rule nevertheless starts metformin in a newly diagnosed patient at any eGFR ≥30. The rule's threshold of 30 matches KDIGO 2022, which allows initiation at half dose at eGFR 30-44. The rule's alt-tier threshold of 45 matches the label's initiation limit.
notes: VERIFIER: Re-opened the KDIGO 2022 PDF (PMID 36272764 matches the DOI) and confirmed Rec 4.1.1, Figure 27 ('eGFR < 30 ... Stop metformin; do not initiate metformin'; eGFR 30-44 'Initiate at half the dose'), Rec 1.3.1, Rec 4.2.1 and Figure 23. Re-opened the Glucophage PDF (Rev April 2017, Reference ID 4079189, distributed by Bristol-Myers Squibb) and the Januvia SPL (effective 2024-11-14, version 71); all quotes match. Changes: (1) The claim that 'when metformin cannot be used, KDIGO prefers an SGLT2 inhibitor' was inaccurate. Rec 1.3.1 recommends an SGLT2i for T2D with CKD and eGFR ≥20 regardless of metformin; the simplification is rewritten. (2) Added that a GLP-1 RA is the preferred agent at eGFR <30, per KDIGO Figure 23 and ADA Standards of Care 2026 Rec 9.11. Source: '9. Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026', Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1):S183-S215, doi:10.2337/dc26-S009, PMID 41358900, PMC12690185 (opened). Sitagliptin is therefore allowed but not preferred. (3) Added a simplification for the metformin-only default. 'History of fever (over 38 degrees Celsius)' becomes a current measured temperature above 38.0 C (current only). A fever reported earlier in this illness, with a normal temperature now, counts under Centor but not under the rule.
'Tonsillar exudate' and 'tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy or lymphadenitis' become current findings ('tender anterior cervical lymph nodes').
NICE allows either FeverPAIN or Centor. The rule uses Centor items only.

Antibiotic arm: for Centor 3 or 4 NICE says 'consider an immediate antibiotic prescription ... or a back-up antibiotic prescription'. The rule turns this into a direct instruction to prescribe penicillin V now and drops the back-up option.

Default arm: NICE says 'Consider paracetamol for pain or fever, or if preferred and suitable, ibuprofen'. The rule makes ibuprofen, NICE's second-named option, the default for everyone below the cutoff and drops paracetamol.
The two arms are mutually exclusive in the rule ('instead'). In NICE, self-care analgesia applies to everyone with acute sore throat, including people who get an antibiotic.
The drug is named penicillin V (phenoxymethylpenicillin). NICE's adult dose and course length (500 mg four times a day or 1,000 mg twice a day for 5 to 10 days) are not stated.

Penicillin allergy or intolerance is not addressed. NICE Table 1 gives clarithromycin as the alternative first choice (erythromycin in pregnancy), while the rule prescribes penicillin V to everyone at or above the cutoff.

contradictions: A patient with a cough and exactly two of the three rule criteria has a Centor score of 2. For that score NICE NG84 says 'Do not offer an antibiotic prescription', but the rule prescribes penicillin V. The rule agrees with NICE when cough is absent, and the fixed setting ('Sore throat for two days.') does not say whether the patient has a cough.
